In at least one embodiment, an orchestrator conversational AI receives input(s), and uses one or more strategies to obtain one or more results from one or more expert conversational AIs based in part on one or more inputs received by the orchestrator conversational AI, and determines at least one response to the one or more inputs based at least on a portion of the one or more results.

sources.title: MODELED CONVERSIONS FOR A CONNECTION NETWORK SYSTEM [US20260278339A1]
sources.abstract: Modeled conversions for connection networking are described. A method comprises generating a first input vector comprising a set of sequence features for a group of entities using a transformer layer of a machine learning model, generating a second input vector comprising a set of identity profile features for the group of entities using a generative artificial intelligence layer, receiving a third input vector comprising a set of conversion features, concatenating the first input vector, the second input vector, and the third input vector into a concatenated vector, normalizing the concatenated vector to form a normalized vector, projecting the normalized vector to form a projected vector, and generating a first metric based on the projected vector using a multi-gate mixture-of-experts (MMOE) layer of the ML model, the first metric comprising a value indicating whether there is a deterministic entity level conversion event for a group level conversion event.

sources.title: Hybrid expert model-oriented multi-core grain reasoning acceleration method, system and application [CN122759239A]
authors: SHANGHAI QUSU CHAOWEI TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: SHANGHAI QUSU CHAOWEI TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a mixed expert model-oriented multi-core grain reasoning acceleration method, which comprises the following steps of: for an input token sequence, constructing distribution mapping from a token to a target core grain in a current MoE layer according to a target expert selected for the input token by a gating network; the token embedding corresponding to each token is broadcasted and distributed along the annular interconnection topology, so that the target core particle receives and caches the token embedding corresponding to the local expert; each target core grain executes calculation on a target expert hitting the storage range of the core grain based on the cached token embedding and the expert weight stored in the core grain to obtain the partial sum of the corresponding token; the parts corresponding to the same token are aggregated along the annular interconnection topology, and the layer output embedding of the current MoE layer is obtained; monitoring the load of each calculation core particle, and dynamically adjusting the distribution mapping of the next MoE layer according to the load statistical information. draft.summary: Research and patent activity on mixture of experts (MoE) is rising fast. Papers matching the topic phrases grew from 748 in 2024 to 2,306 in 2025, and 5,282 were published by 19 Oct 2026 against 1,618 a year earlier. Patent filings are also rising, with 333 by the same date in 2026 against 188 in 2025 [P1-P6]. Social-media posts report a cluster of large MoE model releases [X1, X4], but these are unverified. The only filing-based commercial evidence is a very small company with a large net loss [M1-M3]. Risk findings show routing and expert collapse, fragile dense-to-sparse conversion, and efficiency gains that depend on hardware and scale [R1-R6, S9]. Several supportive science findings were also challenged as over-generalised from single preprints [C1-C7]. The main uncertainty is whether MoE's efficiency promise holds up in real training and serving, and whether that turns into revenue.
draft.plain_summary: Mixture of experts is a way of building AI models in which only a small part of a very large model works on each request, which can save computing cost. Research and patent filings are growing very fast, and several large model releases were reported this week, but those reports are unconfirmed and there is little proof of paying customers yet. The main thing that could stop it is that these models can be unstable to train and the savings depend heavily on the hardware and setup.

themes.name: MoE inference efficiency and hardware co-design

horizons.label: forecast
horizons.assessment: Papers propose pruning, caching, and topology-aware routing to cut MoE serving cost [S2, S3, S8]. Patents on parallelism and accelerators are numerous [P1, P3]. Reported gains are author-reported best cases, mostly from single preprints [C3, C4], and serving gains depend on hardware and regime [R5]. An unverified social post mentions NVIDIA and Inferact submitting a Rubin NVL72 inference result [X5]. Evidence supports active effort, not proven general savings.

horizons.label: forecast
horizons.assessment: If inference methods generalise beyond single-GPU or small-scale tests, hardware-aware MoE serving could become a differentiator. The patent trend is rising [P1]. Naive implementations gave no speedup in one small vision study [S9, C7]. The evidence does not show that gains survive at frontier scale.

horizons.label: assumption
horizons.assessment: The cited evidence says almost nothing about this horizon. Any view depends on assumptions about hardware roadmaps, which no finding addresses beyond a single unverified social post [X5].

bull.label: forecast
bull.narrative: Pruning, caching and topology-aware routing generalise to large models and commodity hardware, and the patent activity on accelerators and parallelism [P1, P3] becomes products that lower serving costs.

base.label: forecast
base.narrative: Efficiency gains are real but conditional on hardware, batch regime and implementation [R5, S9]. Progress is incremental and specific to each deployment, with filings continuing to grow [P1].

bear.label: forecast
bear.narrative: The headline gains (up to 93.72% memory reduction, 10x throughput) prove to be best cases against weak baselines with unreported quality cost [C3, C4]. Memory-bound serving erodes the compute savings [R5], and patents prove to be defensive filings rather than revenue.

The claim that routing is the 'dominant problem' is a sampling artefact, not a measured share [C1]. Near-term outcomes are dominated by engineering workarounds.

bear.label: forecast
